articles.title: GJ 3378b: A Rocky World Right Next Door — But Is It Habitable?
articles.summary: Astronomers have refined the details of GJ 3378b, a rocky exoplanet just 25 light-years away. It's now confirmed to be a super-Earth in its star's habitable zone, but intense radiation might have stripped its atmosphere. We'll need a future telescope to know if it's truly livable.

articles.title: The Accidental Neuron: How a Forgotten Wire Could Slash AI's Energy Appetite
articles.summary: A student's oversight in the lab revealed that a standard transistor can mimic a biological neuron when its bulk terminal is left unconnected. This discovery could enable neuromorphic chips with single-device neurons and synapses, drastically cutting the power needed for AI.

articles.title: Anemones' Antiviral Paradox: The Protein That Fights Viruses by Slamming the Brakes
articles.summary: A newly discovered protein in sea anemones, CARDIB, suppresses immune responses yet is crucial for antiviral defense. Removing it made anemones far more vulnerable to viruses, revealing an evolutionary strategy opposite to the human MAVS pathway.
